title: On-Prem / Air-Gapped Validation Plan — Private Observability Minimum Pack (v1)
content:
Document purpose
This document is the end-to-end validation plan for the Redwood Private “observability minimum pack” in on-prem / air-gapped environments. It is intended to be executable by Engineering + SRE + PS in a lab environment that simulates common customer constraints (no outbound internet, image mirroring, restricted network policies, limited storage classes). It focuses on: (1) offline artifact/bundle verification, (2) install + post-install signal verification, (3) simulated upgrade + rollback, and (4) failure injection checks for the highest-impact observability failure modes.

Background / why this exists
We have had multiple cases where private installs were “successful” but observability was partially missing or broke on upgrade (e.g., dashboards not included in airgap bundle, Prometheus scrape blocked by NetworkPolicy, noisy rules after version bump). The minimum pack is only “supported” if it works without bespoke setup and survives upgrades/rollbacks with clear operator guidance.

Scope
In scope
- Air-gapped delivery of observability artifacts and images: dashboards, alert rules, recording rules, log collector config, any sidecar/configmap templates, and installer manifests.
- Installer/Helm flows that ship the minimum pack with Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) with emphasis on on-prem.
- Post-install validation steps: Prometheus scrapes, Grafana datasource health, dashboards rendering, alert rules loaded, log collection present.
- Upgrade and rollback of:
  - redwood-private-installer
  - redwood-helm-charts values
  - observability-pack bundle versions (dashboards/rules)
- Failure injection to validate that dashboards/alerts/rules behave as designed and that runbooks are actionable.

Out of scope (v1)
- Customer-specific SIEM deployments beyond “documented export works in lab” for one target.
- Full trace pipeline validation (if traces are best-effort in v1); we only validate that any shipped trace hooks do not break install.
- Long retention / multi-cluster federation / premium dashboards.

Owners / roles
- Primary owner: Fatima Noor (on-prem/air-gapped requirements)
- Packaging/release: Connor O’Brien (bundle manifest + release branch/backports)
- Installer/Helm: Diego Santos (installer and chart wiring)
- SRE validation sign-off: Rafael Mendes (pager readiness + alert noise)
- CI automation: Sahana Iyer (smoke test harness integration, where feasible)
- PS review: Bruno Silva (customer install constraints)

Test environments
We will validate against two reference environments:
A) “Strict airgap lab” (preferred)
- K8s: RKE2 or kubeadm (1.27–1.29 range), single control-plane + 2 worker nodes
- No outbound internet from cluster nodes (egress blocked at firewall)
- Private registry available inside the network (Harbor or ECR-compatible)
- NetworkPolicies enabled (default deny for namespaces that support it)
- Storage: one default StorageClass + one “slow” class (to emulate customer NFS)

B) “Semi-airgap / staging on-prem-like”
- K8s on cloud VMs but with outbound blocked to simulate airgap
- Can re-run quickly for iteration

Baseline versions under test (fill in per run)
- Redwood Private installer version: __
- Helm chart version: __
- Observability pack bundle version: __
- Prometheus/Grafana versions (if packaged/required): __

Entry criteria
- Offline bundle is produced by release process and includes:
  - bundle manifest (files + checksums)
  - container image list + digests
  - dashboards bundle JSON
  - Prometheus rules YAML
  - log collector configuration (values + templates)
  - installation instructions (operator-facing)
- Installer supports an explicit “offline mode” or documented steps for air-gapped installation.
- Preflight checks implemented for storage/network/resources (or known limitations documented).

Exit criteria (GA readiness gate for airgapped)
All “P0” validations pass in Strict airgap lab:
P0
- Bundle verification passes (manifest checksums/digests match; no missing artifacts).
- Clean install completes with no outbound internet.
- Post-install checks confirm:
  - Prometheus scrapes Redwood targets (control plane + runtime) successfully.
  - Grafana is reachable and Redwood dashboards render non-empty after generating synthetic traffic.
  - Alert rules and recording rules are loaded (Prometheus rule groups present).
  - Logs from core components are captured by default collector and visible at the chosen sink (at least one of: Loki in-cluster OR file buffer + documented forwarder; see log section).
- Upgrade path N -> N+1 works offline; dashboards/rules still load; no hard break in metric names without a documented migration.
- Rollback N+1 -> N works offline and restores prior dashboards/rules/config without leaving cluster broken.

P1
- Failure injection confirms at least 6 key alerts fire correctly (and resolve) and runbook steps lead to diagnosis.
- Known noisy alerts are disabled by default (if applicable) or thresholds are tuned for private footprints.

Artifacts to verify (offline bundle content)
1) Bundle manifest integrity
- Verify bundle contains a manifest file listing every artifact with SHA256.
- Verify SHA256 checksums match for:
  - dashboards tar/zip (or raw JSON bundle)
  - rules YAML
  - values/templates for log collector
  - any preflight/postinstall scripts
- Verify manifest is versioned and references the same release tag as installer and charts.

2) Container image completeness
- Validate the image list includes every image required for the “minimum supported” install, including:
  - Grafana (if we ship it or require it via chart)
  - Prometheus (if we ship it or require it via chart)
  - log collector/forwarder (e.g., promtail/vector/fluent-bit—whichever is the chosen default)
  - Redwood control plane images
  - Redwood runtime/serving images
  - any exporters (node-exporter, kube-state-metrics) if included
- For each image:
  - verify digest pinning (sha256:...)
  - verify the mirrored registry references match customer instructions

3) Dashboard bundle correctness
- Confirm bundle includes at minimum:
  - Runtime Overview dashboard
  - Control Plane Health dashboard
  - Infra/GPU overview panels (if part of minimum set)
- Validate dashboard JSON loads into Grafana without plugin dependencies not included in the bundle.
- Confirm dashboard variables do not require high-cardinality labels (avoid model/tenant/route exploding).

4) Prometheus rules correctness
- Validate rules YAML parses (`promtool check rules`).
- Validate rule group names are stable and namespaced (avoid collisions).
- Ensure alert annotations include:
  - summary
  - description
  - runbook URL (internal) or runbook reference string for on-prem docs

Air-gapped install validation (clean install)
Plan: validate a clean install in Strict airgap lab.

Steps
1) Prepare mirrored registry
- Import all images from bundle image list into internal registry.
- Validate pull works from cluster nodes.

2) Prepare cluster prerequisites
- Create namespaces per installer expectations.
- Ensure default StorageClass exists.
- Apply baseline NetworkPolicies (default deny) in a way that matches “typical secure customer posture,” then explicitly allow required traffic per documented policy.

3) Run installer in offline mode
- Execute installer with offline bundle path (or offline flags).
- Confirm installer does not attempt to reach external endpoints (watch for DNS queries / connection attempts).
- Validate preflight checks:
  - storage availability
  - required ports/services
  - resource requests fit within node capacity
  - scrape endpoints reachable (post-install)

4) Generate traffic
- Run a synthetic load job (small) against the private API gateway to produce baseline metrics/logs.
- Minimum: sustained requests for 10 minutes to populate time series.

5) Post-install verification checklist
Prometheus
- Prometheus UI reachable (or via port-forward).
- Targets page shows “UP” for:
  - runtime/serving pods
  - API gateway
  - policy/routing service
  - installer/upgrade controller (if metrics exist)
- Confirm presence of key metrics (examples; update to actual names when finalized):
  - request rate and error rate (recording rules preferred)
  - latency histograms/quantiles (p95/p99)
  - GPU utilization or saturation signals
  - queue depth/backpressure signals
Grafana
- Grafana UI reachable.
- Datasource to Prometheus is healthy (no auth errors).
- Dashboards appear under a consistent folder (e.g., “Redwood Private”).
- Dashboards render non-empty panels after traffic generation.
Alert rules
- Prometheus “Rules” page shows rule groups loaded and evaluated.
- No constant-evaluating failing rules due to missing metrics (unless documented as optional).
Logs
- Confirm at least these components produce logs to collector:
  - API gateway
  - routing/policy engine
  - runtime pods
  - installer/controller
- Confirm log lines are structured and include expected fields (non-sensitive):
  - timestamp
  - level
  - component
  - request_id (or correlation id)
  - model/route fields only if cardinality-safe and redacted/sampled appropriately
- Confirm no secrets/PII are present in logs by default (spot-check for auth headers, tokens, prompt payloads).

Upgrade validation (offline)
Goal: ensure upgrades do not break dashboards/alerts/log pipeline and do not require internet access.

Upgrade matrix
- Primary: N -> N+1 (last stable release to current candidate)
- Secondary: N-1 -> N (if time permits)

Procedure
1) Snapshot baseline
- Record versions of:
  - installer
  - chart
  - observability bundle
- Export:
  - Grafana dashboard list (names/ids)
  - Prometheus rule group list
  - Prometheus target status
- Keep copies of values files and ConfigMaps related to observability.

2) Perform upgrade (offline)
- Provide upgraded bundle and images via internal registry.
- Run installer/upgrade controller to apply upgrade.
- Confirm no external calls.

3) Validate post-upgrade
- Re-run post-install verification checklist.
- Specific checks:
  - dashboards still present (no missing folder)
  - new dashboards/rules appear only if expected
  - no duplicate dashboards from failed migration
  - rule groups evaluate cleanly
  - cardinality remains bounded (spot-check series count for top metrics)

4) Regression checks
- Validate the synthetic load still results in expected metric deltas.
- Confirm no critical alerts are firing at steady state unless thresholds are intentionally strict.

Rollback validation (offline)
Goal: ensure rollback restores a known-good state without leaving cluster in a broken partial state.

Procedure
1) Trigger rollback to N
- Use installer rollback mechanics or Helm rollback (as documented).
- Ensure rollback uses locally available bundle artifacts.

2) Validate post-rollback
- Same checklist as clean install.
- Verify:
  - dashboards/rules/config are consistent with N (no leftover N+1 artifacts that cause confusion)
  - Prometheus targets are stable
  - log collector returns to prior configuration

Failure injection tests
We will validate that the minimum pack detects + helps diagnose failures. Each test includes: setup, injection, expected signals, and cleanup.

F1: Prometheus cannot scrape runtime pods (NetworkPolicy regression)
- Inject: apply a restrictive NetworkPolicy blocking Prometheus -> runtime metrics port.
- Expected:
  - Prometheus target goes DOWN within 1–2 scrape intervals
  - Alert fires (severity per policy; likely ticket or page depending on coverage)
  - Dashboard panels indicate missing data (with a clear “no data” state)
- Cleanup: restore allow policy

F2: Grafana datasource auth misconfig (common customer issue)
- Inject: rotate Prometheus auth secret without updating Grafana datasource OR break service DNS.
- Expected:
  - Grafana datasource health fails
  - Dashboard panels show datasource error
  - Alert (if we ship one) indicates Grafana datasource failure OR runbook directs operator to datasource troubleshooting
- Cleanup: restore secret/config

F3: Prometheus storage pressure / TSDB issues
- Inject: reduce PVC size in lab (or fill disk) to force WAL/TSDB errors.
- Expected:
  - Prometheus logs show WAL/TSDB errors
  - Alert fires for disk/pvc pressure
  - Runbook points to retention/PVC sizing guidance
- Cleanup: restore storage / redeploy

F4: Runtime pod restart loop (OOM / crash)
- Inject: constrain runtime memory limit and push load; or force a crash loop.
- Expected:
  - Kubernetes restart count increases
  - Alert for restart loop / OOMKilled fires
  - Dashboard shows elevated error rate/latency and decreased throughput
- Cleanup: restore resources

F5: Elevated error rate (upstream dependency broken)
- Inject: break model registry integration endpoint or simulate 5xx from a critical internal dependency.
- Expected:
  - error rate alert fires (SLO burn if configured)
  - dashboard highlights which component is failing (control plane health panels)
- Cleanup: restore endpoint

F6: Log forwarder backpressure / dropping
- Inject: throttle log sink (e.g., block egress to sink or reduce sink capacity) and generate high logs.
- Expected:
  - log forwarder metrics show retries/backpressure
  - alert (if shipped) indicates log pipeline degradation OR runbook describes how to detect dropping
  - cluster resource usage remains bounded (forwarder doesn’t OOM the node)
- Cleanup: restore sink + verify recovery

What to record during each failure injection
- timestamps of injection start/end
- which alerts fired (name, severity, time to fire, time to resolve)
- screenshots or exports of affected dashboards
- key logs from Prometheus/Grafana/log forwarder
- notes: was runbook actionable? any missing “what to do first” steps?

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
- Offline bundle validation: 0 missing artifacts; checksums match; image list complete.
- Installation: completes in airgap with no manual patching beyond documented prerequisites.
- Observability basics:
  - For each in-scope component, at least one metric confirms liveness/health.
  - Golden signals available for runtime request path: rate, errors, latency, saturation.
  - Dashboards load with meaningful defaults and do not require per-customer edits.
- Upgrades/rollbacks:
  - no empty dashboards due to broken variables
  - no alert storms introduced by upgrade at steady state
  - metric naming changes are backwards-compatible or explicitly migrated
- Security:
  - no secrets/PII logged by default (spot check is not exhaustive; security review tracked separately)
  - any identifiers are hashed/limited as per standards

Deliverables / outputs
- Validation report (per run):
  - environment details
  - versions tested
  - pass/fail checklist
  - issues found + severity + owner
  - suggested fixes (PR references)
- Known issues updates: add validated workarounds to Support-facing doc.
- If feasible: convert P0 checks to automated smoke tests (ENG-19156) in CI for nightly coverage (semi-airgap environment).

Risks / open questions
- Do we ship Prometheus/Grafana as part of the minimum pack for on-prem, or only provide integration guidance? This affects what “offline bundle” must contain.
- If log export sink is external (Splunk/ELK), how do we validate in Strict airgap lab without standing up the sink? Proposed: validate in-cluster Loki as default and optionally validate one external sink in Semi-airgap.
- NetworkPolicy templates: do we provide “known-good” policies or only documentation? Customers frequently run default-deny; validation will assume we provide a path.
- Metric cardinality: we should add a lightweight check during validation (e.g., top series count) to catch accidental label explosions.

Next actions
- Connor: confirm bundle manifest format and where checksums live (installer vs separate file).
- Diego: confirm offline install path and flags for airgapped mode; ensure preflight failures are clear.
- Rafael: finalize which alerts are P0 vs P1 for airgapped GA gate.
- Sahana: propose which of the P0 validations can be automated in smoke tests without requiring full airgap.

Notes to self (Fatima)
- When we run the first Strict airgap pass, prioritize catching missing artifacts (dashboards/rules) and outbound calls. Those are the most expensive to debug late.
- Capture evidence for “no outbound calls” (tcpdump logs or firewall logs) to reduce future argument with security teams.
